articles.title: LEGO PlayStation Is Now Available
articles.summary: LEGO PlayStation is now available for LEGO Insiders, and it comes with a free Astro Bot Set. Here's how to become and Insider for free.
articles.body:
Update Oct 5: The LEGO PlayStation set is now available to purchase for anyone, Insider or not ( see it at LEGO ). Unfortunately, the LEGO Astro Bot sold out and no longer comes with it. However , LEGO has made the Darth Vader's Lightsaber set (valued at $29.99) free with purchase of LEGO PlayStation.

Good news, retro gaming fans: the LEGO set based on the original PlayStation console is now available ( see it at LEGO ). The only catch is that you need to be a LEGO Insider to buy it. Thankfully, you can sign up for free right here . LEGO PlayStation costs $179.99, and it comes with LEGO Astro Bot as a free Gift with Purchase.

If you aren’t a LEGO Insider and you refuse to sign up for a free account for some reason, you’ll be able to buy LEGO PlayStation starting October 4. It’s possible it will sell out quickly, and it’s also possible LEGO Astro Bot will sell out. So if you want to make sure you get one, you’ll want to sign up for the (again, free) LEGO Insiders program .

LEGO PlayStation is a near 1:1 scale set of Sony’s original gaming console, which came out in 1994 in Japan and 1995 in the US. It includes the console as well as the original no-analog-sticks PlayStation controller (the DualShock wouldn’t arrive until three years later).

As with most pricy LEGO sets for adults , the LEGO PS1 has some fun Easter eggs to find. First of all, set's box calls back to the box the original PlayStation came in, which is pretty great. The set's Power and Open buttons actually work. Pressing Power flips a green LEGO piece into view underneath it, as if you were turning it on. The Open button releases the disc cover, letting you see two dioramas hidden inside.

The dioramas are based on Gran Turismo (1997) and Ape Escape (1999). These dioramas can also be removed from the set to display on their own (though that leaves a hole on either side of the PS1 model).

As for LEGO Astro Bot, it's a free Gift With Purchase, but you'll be able to buy it separately at PlayStation Direct for $24.99.

For more about new and future sets, check out all the upcoming LEGO set release dates . And if you want more LEGO sets based on video games, check out our picks for the best Nintendo LEGO sets .

Chris Reed is a senior commerce editor and deals expert for IGN. He also runs IGN's LEGO coverage and maintains the upcoming release dates articles for video games , LEGO sets , and 4K Blu-rays . You can follow him on Bluesky .

articles.title: Rockstar Traveled Across Florida With Gang Members and Cops for GTA 6 Research
articles.summary: Rockstar has discussed travelling across Florida with gang members and cops for GTA 6 research, and hovering in a helicopter above a Beyonce concert.
articles.body:
Love Magazine recently got an exclusive interview with Rockstar Games ahead of GTA 6 ’s release next month. While the interview focuses primarily on the love story between dual protagonists Jason and Lucia, there’s some interesting insight into the studio’s process for creating the most impressive virtual worlds ever made.

For its rendition of Florida, team members spent lots of time embedding with the culture and exploring the landscape of Miami and its surrounding areas. These research trips start small as the leads scout out the most interesting locations and stories, and more team members come on subsequent trips to dive deeper into the culture, stories, and people.

“Every game we make starts with research trips. It’s where to get to explore both the place and our ideas as a group,” head of development Aaron Garbut said. “To begin, a small group of us spent some time traveling from Miami through some of the surrounding towns and through the Florida Keys down to Key West. This is one of the best parts of the entire project: a car full of friends, driving for days on end, talking about what we want to make and being immersed in the locations and our ideas.”

Grand Theft Auto 6 vs Real Life Inspiration

Garbut takes a camera and a phone and records everything that happens. During one shoot, a handful of Rockstar devs spent the day flying low and fast over mangrove inlets in the everglades, before ending the day hovering over a stadium with a live Beyonce concert playing. “I think we made the local news that day,” Garbut said.

“We do go in-depth, we hang with locals and we hear lots of stories and learn as much as we can. We travel around with cops and with gang members. Everyone is lovely. Some people are equally scary. We experience the underside as well; although the people who showed us around were among the nicest we’ve met, the stories, the places, the details could be terrifying. We try to build a world that is believable and varied, with depth, so that is the research we need.

“Miami itself is really those extremes — lovely people, incredible wealth, incredible poverty, excess, craziness, the hustle, and showing it all off. That’s our research trips — experiencing those extremes so that we can bring them into our world, and it all finds its way into the game in surprising ways.”

Some of those surprising ways could be pedestrian dialogue or radio shows and advertisements, which Rockstar said it doesn’t treat as secondary content. Everything is important when creating a world you want players to spend hundreds of hours exploring.

Rockstar’s approach to a GTA game set in the modern day is to deliberately avoid recreating real-world viral moments, since long development timelines mean these kinds of references can date a game — ask Borderlands. Instead, GTA 6’s satire focuses on modern culture, conspiracy theories, and “the strange ways people react to events.”

Last week, local team the Miami Heat announced a special match, during which the Heat will wear a GTA 6 uniform in a themed arena. We've got extensive coverage of GTA 6 across IGN. Check out IGN's interview with Rockstar Games , our GTA 6 preview , and word of the first confirmed GTA 6 voice actor .

articles.title: 'The Movie Still Hasn't Made Any Money': Dakota Johnson is Happy to Joke About Madame Web Being One of Hollywood's Worst Ever Flops
articles.summary: Madame Web star Dakota Johnson has joked about her widely-panned superhero movie's status as a box office bomb.
articles.body:
Madame Web star Dakota Johnson has joked about her widely-panned superhero movie's status as a box office bomb.

Appearing as the host of this week's Saturday Night Live , Johnson humorously noted that she had last fronted the show back in 2024 while promoting the Spider-Man spinoff. And now, she continued, she was still trying to promote Madame Web — as the movie was still trying to turn a profit.

"The last time I was here I was promoting a movie called Madame Web, thank you," Johnson said to muted applause. "And tonight I'm still promoting it because the movie still hasn't made any money yet."

Ranking the Phase 4 Marvel Movies and Shows From Worst to Best

Madame Web is infamously bad, even in a run of films from Sony that also includes Morbius and Venom 3. It made $100.5 million at the box office from a gross budget of $100 million (although factoring in distributor costs is believed to still made a loss). It was also a disaster critically: the subject of widespread memes online and a 10% approval on Rotten Tomatoes. It later scooped three Golden Raspberry awards, including Worst Actress for Johnson herself.

While the film did not make a lot of cash, Madame Web is a long way from ranking among Hollywood's worst box office bombs — or even the worst-performing comic book movie. Disney's John Carter is widely-regarded as the biggest commercial failure of all time, losing up to $200 million. Disney's The Lone Ranger lost up to $190 million, meanwhile. Just behind those was The Marvels, which lost a similar amount and remains the worst-performing comic book movie ever — a fate Madame Web avoided by being far cheaper to make.

"Madame Web has the makings of an interesting hybrid," we wrote in IGN's Madame Web review , which returned a 5/10 score. "But with a script overcrowded with extraneous characters, basic archetypes, and generic dialogue, it fails the talent and the future of its onscreen Spider-Women."

Earlier this year, Sony Pictures boss Tom Rothman acknowledged that "the audience wasn't satisfied enough" with its live-action Spider-Man spinoff movies. Starting with Hardy's Venom in 2018, the full roster included that film, Venom: Let There Be Carnage , Morbius, Madame Web, Venom: The Last Dance , and Kraven the Hunter. Sony had, at one point, planned to integrate Spider-Man into the villain-led offshoots, though such a crossover never came to fruition .

articles.title: Best Buy’s Techtober Sale Challenges Prime Day with Major Video Game Deals and No Membership Fees
articles.summary: Best Buy's Techtober sale is now live, rivalling Amazon Prime Day with savings on new PS5 game releases, Xbox hardware bundles, and plenty more.
articles.body:
Best Buy has launched its Techtober sale , a direct competitor to Amazon's latest Prime-exclusive sale, Prime Big Deal Days. Techtober is running until October 11 and includes plenty of deals and discounts on, you guessed it, Tech, video games, home appliances, and more.

There are some fairly standout offers up for grabs, so I'll leave a few of my favorite picks just below. Otherwise, feel free to take a look and browse the full sale yourself.

Nintendo Switch 2 + Mario Kart World Bundle

Highlights for me, of course, are the decent variety of video games included in the new sale. Standouts include the critically acclaimed Star Wars: Zero Company for both PS5 and Xbox. It's down to $47.99, $12 off its list price, and its first discount since launch.

There's also LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Night, down to $59.99 , and $10 off for both PS5 and Xbox. That's alongside Battlefield 6, a gaming highlight from last year, down to just $34.99 , which is a pretty excellent deal!

Obviously, Best Buy is also highlighting the Nintendo Switch 2 Mario Kart World bundle in the sale, even if it isn't technically a sale item. You can save $37.97 if you buy this bundle, versus buying the console and game separately. It's certainly not as good as the bundle deal we saw for the Switch 2 at launch, but considering the price of those bad boys has gone up this year (along with everything else, am I right?), it's still not a bad offering and worth calling out nonetheless.

XBOX Series X 1TB Digital Console Bundle

Another interesting offer, albeit significantly more expensive than everything else I've mentioned, is the Gears of War E-Day Xbox Series X bundle that's up for grabs . It's listed for $819.97, and includes a 1TB Xbox Series X digital console (MSRP $749.99), a digital copy of Gears of War E-Day (MSRP $69.99), and a slick transparent red Xbox Elite Series 2 controller (MSRP $149.99).

Overall savings are $150, and while it's not a bad deal, it's still expensive and probably only going to appeal to a select few. At $820, this will be a tough ask for a lot of us, and while I'm cautious to give any kind of financial advice, Best Buy does offer the option to pay over 12 months at $68.34/mo as well, just so you are aware.

Overall, the bundle is worth considering if you are okay with digital-only gaming (especially with Xbox allowing you to digitise your game discs now ), and are looking for a way to play GTA 6 and the critically acclaimed Gears of War E-Day .

All the big US retailers like to go toe-to-toe during massive sale seasons (like the one we are in now, which will continue all the way through to New Year's Day 2027), and Best Buy is no different.

But what are the major differences between the two sales, and is it worth shopping one over the other?

Well, for starters, Best Buy's sale isn't locked behind a membership. While there are still some specific deals that are exclusive to Best Buy's premium membership, the vast majority of deals are not.

Additionally, Best Buy's sale is running until October 11, while Amazon's Prime Big Deal Days sale starts October 6 and runs through 11:59 PM on October 7. So, Best Buy's sale is significantly longer and will give you a bit more opportunity to shop around or make a decision on your purchases.

Apple AirPods Pro 3 Wireless Noise Canceling Earbuds

When it comes to which sale to shop, I'd advise just going wherever has the best deals. For example, while Best Buy has some great offers, Amazon has a better deal on the Apple AirPods Pro 3. The premium earbuds are down to $179 at Amazon, but $199.99 at Best Buy.

Amazon will also often price match the vast majority of other retailers, without you even having to ask. So if you've got a Prime membership and want to shop there, go ahead. As long as you're saving money and being savvy when hunting down bargains, you're in the clear.

Should You Shop Best Buy’s Techtober Sale or Wait for Black Friday?

Honestly? Probably, yeah. While Amazon's October Prime Day sale ( Prime Big Deal Days ) is a good opportunity to grab a few good deals, more often than not these offers will reappear in a month or less, as they were, or as even better deals. If you can hold out, I'll always recommend waiting a little bit longer in order to save that bit more.

That being said, there is a rare chance that certain deals appear that are worth picking up ASAP. I, and the rest of my team, will often try to call these bargains out as and when we can, so you have the best opportunity to bag them. Otherwise, consider the rest of this article a helpful guide to what's on sale, what you can pick up if you so choose to, and the prices to look for when the Black Friday sales eventually roll around in November.

The only other reason I'd ever suggest not waiting is if you value your time over your money. Now it seems like an obvious statement, but it's not always a luxury we all get to have. If you do desperately want to play that game like right now and it's driving you insane, or your TV just broke, or you lost your headphones, sales like this are a great opportunity to pay yourself in time, so you don't have to stress or fret about something. Whatever the case, do what is best for you. I'm just a silly little guy, writing about silly little deals, on a silly little website.

Robert Anderson is a Senior Commerce Editor for IGN. Based in London, UK, he is a qualified journalist with a Bachelor of Arts in Journalism (First Class Degree) and over seven years of professional writing and editing experience.

You can usually find Robert lost in open-world RPG games like Elden Ring and Cyberpunk 2077. Outside of gaming, his passions include reading comics (especially Superman, Batman, and Spider-Man), taking photos, and keeping up with the latest in film and TV.

His primary coverage focuses on tracking down the best gaming deals and diving into the fast-paced world of Trading Card Games (TCGs). He regularly covers everything from the latest releases in Pokémon TCG and the most expensive cards to comprehensive Magic: The Gathering buying guides .

articles.title: Doctor Who Ex-Showrunner Says He's Not Bothered About Walking Away With His Cliffhanger Ending Left Unresolved
articles.summary: Doctor Who ex-showrunner Russell T Davies has described his unresolved cliffhanger ending as "a piece of p***" for the series' next production team to resolve.
articles.body:
Doctor Who ex-showrunner Russell T Davies has described his unresolved cliffhanger ending as "a piece of p***" for the series' next production team to resolve, following his departure from the franchise amid clear frustrations over plot leaks.

Davies' tenure as the head writer of Doctor Who officially ended this summer when the BBC finally admitted that it (plus Davies and production company Bad Wolf) were no longer planning a final Christmas special to wrap up the show's current era . This followed the collapse of Disney's co-production deal after two seasons, and significant reshoots to navigate the exit of series star Ncuti Gatwa.

Doctor Who now sits in limbo as the BBC searches for a fresh production company to take the series forward . And, in the meantime, Davies has now published his first account of what happened as his time on the show came to an end.

In an excerpt from his upcoming memoir The Queerest of Folk: A Life in Television published by The Guardian , Davies said that the future of the Disney co-production deal was unclear when he was writing the second season.

"That was nothing to do with us at Bad Wolf; it was down to conversations with Disney and the BBC," Davies wrote. "So we had no idea what was going on. Deep down I thought it wouldn't. You could tell what I was thinking, because I was already creating new work," he added, listing off a couple of other projects that he had already begun planning for other broadcasters.

"In some ways it would have been a nightmare for me if that third series had come along, but I would have managed it," he continued. "As the third series was in flux, the finale was intended to climax with an open-ended regeneration. So we shot that with Ncuti: he smiled and said his last line, and the screen melted into a golden glow... Except when we edited that together, it looked like the death of the show. We said, 'Think of children watching that. It's like a death. We can’t do that to them.'"

There's a lot to unpack here, but first it's worth noting what Davies has not discussed — the fact that the second season finale was initially something else entirely before Gatwa's regeneration was shot. On-set reports, leaked images and actor interviews have all discussed that the season was set to end on a positive note, with a party featuring the show's main cast being observed by original Doctor Who actress Carol Ford, who played the Doctor's granddaughter Susan.

The 25 Most Essential Doctor Who Episodes

Davies has not discussed what happened here to prompt the need to film Gatwa's exit — something that required a rewrite of the episode's ending and reshoots in order to film. There's also no sense of Davies himself or Bad Wolf being in any way responsible for the Disney deal's collapse. Rather, Davies paints the matter as a business decision between Disney and the BBC — which it was, but likely one judged against the success of the show Davies and Bad Wolf delivered.

Finally, there's the sense that an open-ended regeneration sequence would have acted "like a death" for the show. This is going to be a matter of personal taste, but what we got instead — the promise of a big reveal for why Billie Piper appeared, and a Christmas special — has arguably been more painful.

"When it came to announce the end of the Disney deal, the BBC was very keen to announce the existence of a Christmas Special for 2026 at the same time, to confirm its dedication to the show," Davies wrote, discussing his final episode that, ultimately, never came to be.

"Now, I had my doubts, right from the start," Davies claimed, "a Christmas Special about what, who for, where's the money coming from? – but for the first time in my life, I allowed my name to go on a press release that I actually felt kind of queasy about. That'll teach me!"

One other interesting point to note here is Davies acknowledging the show's current status of being put out to tender had been discussed internally already, though was expected to "lurk somewhere in the future, maybe 2028 or 2029." This would fit with previous fan expectations that Davies was due to deliver four years of Doctor Who (perhaps three seasons and a series of specials, similar to David Tennant's era?) before bowing out.

"Yes, that leaves us with a Billie puzzle, but c'mon, that's easy," Davies wrote, addressing his biggest dangling plot thread. "Doctor Who problems are simple to solve (remember, in 1996, it was proclaimed that the Doctor is half-human – that was fixed by everyone discreetly never mentioning it again). A new production team can either seize hold of that appearance happily, or – and this is more likely – they can explain the event away with exactly seven words. Painless. That's not a problem, that's a piece of piss."

It's worth stating that the Doctor's claimed half-human parentage is one of many fans' biggest plot holes and bugbears from the show's history.

Davies' excerpt concludes with a lengthy airing of his frustrations with a prolific Doctor Who leaker who revealed every key plot beat from the Gatwa era up to a year ahead of transmission. How this leaker gained this information remains a mystery, though their complete accuracy and intimate knowledge of the show's production means they must have been part of a small circle of team members working on the series.

"It's absolutely extraordinary, and I swear it did a lot to destroy the profile of the show," Davies wrote. "It introduces a cynicism among fans, because they're not surprised by anything any more. Their response to a leak is weariness, an instant assumption that whatever has been leaked won't work. They instantly imagine the worst version of it, and then, when they eventually see it, it inevitably confirms their bias. So we had to work for two years knowing that leaks were happening, and yet we were powerless."

While the leaks were damaging, it's fair to state that only a fraction of the series' audience would have likely heard about them. They were discussed on Doctor Who fan forums and reddit boards dedicated specifically to leaks, rather than something shared in the mainstream.

"The BBC managed to track down the person who was putting the information online, but it was a member of the public. They were probably friends with someone at some point in the delivery chain of Doctor Who, and we simply didn't have the legal right to seize that person's emails. I wish we did," Davies wrote. "This was my copyrighted material – why don't I have the legal right to get that person arrested? But the BBC was always very scared of how that would look – a member of the public being prosecuted for simply breaking copyright; it would be like breaking a butterfly on a wheel.

"To this day, we don't know who the leaker was, which made us suspicious of every single person we worked with," Davies concluded. "There were some tricky conversations at work. But somewhere down the line, all these episodes go through a hundred technical processes in a hundred different suites, and I'm quite sure it’s just some random person sitting in the back of a room – not the person in charge, but the person whose job it is just to press play on every single thing we ever did, who'd then tell his mate, who'd then post it online. That person is still out there. They might be reading this and frothing with glee. Well done, mate, enjoy your masturbation."

articles.title: 'I'm Still Here': Marvel Star Mark Ruffalo Says He's Still Playing The Hulk Despite Political Advocacy
articles.summary: Marvel star Mark Ruffalo has said he'll "Hulk out" over political attempts to disrupt voting in the upcoming U.S. midterm elections.
articles.body:
Marvel star Mark Ruffalo has said he'll "Hulk out" over political attempts to disrupt voting in the upcoming U.S. midterm elections, and pointed out that he has kept his MCU role despite his high-profile advocacy.

Speaking at the "Hands Off Our Vote" in New York City on September 4, Ruffalo encouraged voters not to be put off by any potential disruption to voting this year, or be afraid of stepping up to defend voters' constitutional rights.

"They're going to try and stop us from taking our country back and we're not going to let them," Ruffalo began. "Trump, we're not letting you," he continued, before beginning a chant of "hands off our vote."

Ruffalo: Hands off our fucking vote. I’m gonna Hulk out. You won’t like me when I’m angry. Hey, I’m still here. They thought I was out for the count. I’m still here. I’m still playing the Hulk. — Acyn (@Acyn) October 4, 2026

Ruffalo: Hands off our fucking vote. I’m gonna Hulk out. You won’t like me when I’m angry. Hey, I’m still here. They thought I was out for the count. I’m still here. I’m still playing the Hulk.

Ruffalo has long been outspoken on political affairs and environmental issues, and has most recently criticized Paramount for its merger with Warner Bros. Perhaps most notably, the actor has criticized the actions of George W. Bush in the Iraq War, and actions taken by the Israeli army against Palestine since 2014.

"Hands off our f***ing vote," Ruffalo continued. "I'm gonna Hulk out. You won't like me when I'm angry," he added, acknowledging that he had continued to speak out despite any potential risk to his own acting career.

"Hey, I'm still here. They thought I was out for the count. I'm still here. I'm still playing the Hulk. Don't be scared. They want to keep us afraid, their only weapon is our fear. But when we see people step out, we can get courage."

While Ruffalo's role as one of the MCU's most prominent characters has never publicly been called into question, Disney itself has taken flak over the years for political statements made by those it employs, or TV shows and movies it produces. The most prominent example of this in recent times was the temporary suspending of late night host Jimmy Kimmel , which resulted in a loud public backlash . Ruffalo, meanwhile, has previously said he's willing to sacrifice his Hollywood career to continue campaigning for the issues he believes in.

"Our time to brave is coming," he concluded. "They're going to do anything they can to keep us in our homes. They're going to do everything they can to make us feel small. They're going to do anything they can to make us feel lost, to make it feel inevitable. It's not inevitable. We're inevitable. The truth is inevitable."

Ruffalo is currently starring in two enormous Marvel blockbusters: the $2.5 billion-grossing Spider-Man: Brand New Day, and the $2.9 billion-grossing Avengers: Endgame, which features a brand new post-credits scene featuring the Hulk .

articles.title: Star Wars Zero Company Gets Its First Big Discount at Amazon Ahead of Prime Big Deal Days
articles.summary: Star Wars Zero Company has dropped to a new low price at Amazon ahead of the retailer's Prime Big Deal Days sale event, with a 20% discount across PS5 and Xbox Series X.
articles.body:
Star Wars Zero Company , one of our favorite games of the year so far , has just received its first big discount since its launch in late August. Ahead of the retailer's Prime Big Deal Days sale , which starts up tomorrow, Amazon has slashed 20% off both PS5 and Xbox Series X physical copies of the game, dropping them down to $47.97 and $47.99, respectively.

That saves you $12 (or just over, if you opt for the PS5 copy) compared to paying full price, which isn't bad at all. Considering this marks a new all-time low price for both the PS5 and Xbox Series X versions at the retailer, it's a great time to grab them. Plus, they're not marked as Early Prime Deals, either, so you don't have to be a Prime member to save on them.

If this XCOM-style strategy game set in a galaxy far, far away has been on your fall wishlist, it's one we'd highly recommend grabbing for your gaming library. Writer Dan Stapleton wrote in IGN's 9/10 review that it's "an excellent tactical game that does a fantastic job of slathering on the same cinematic look and feel we saw in Respawn's Star Wars Jedi games, incorporating strong characters and a storyline that's refreshingly centered on non-Force users and a non-traditional villain."

Amazon isn't the only place that has it discounted, either. As part of its Techtober Sale , Best Buy has also knocked it down to $47.99 across PS5 and Xbox Series X. So, if you'd prefer to scoop it up there, that's another option worth checking out.

The Techtober Sale is stacked with even more game deals to look at alongside Star Wars Zero Company, too. If you're in the shopping mood, it's worth having a look at what's available while the sale is still live until October 11.

Of course, Prime Big Deal Days is also worth keeping an eye on tomorrow for more video game deals. This sale only runs until October 7, though, so you have a shorter amount of time to pick up the discounted titles that catch your eye.

articles.title: Avengers Star Anthony Mackie Says He'll Film Secret Wars When He's Done on Broadway Playing Macbeth — a Run That Lasts Until July 2027
articles.summary: Marvel star Anthony Mackie has sparked further speculation on the production schedule for Avengers: Secret Wars, which looks set to film — and also release — next year.
articles.body:
Marvel star Anthony Mackie has sparked further speculation on the production schedule for Avengers: Secret Wars , which looks set to film — and also release — next year.

Mackie has now announced he will take on the title role in a new Broadway production of Shakespeare's Macbeth that's set to run in New York until July 2027. Rehearsals begin in February, with previews from late March, Deadline reported.

The news has further raised eyebrows among fans currently tracking Marvel's plans to shoot next year's Avengers: Doomsday follow-up, Avengers: Secret Wars — an enormous blockbuster that is now just over a year from release and is also still to begin its principal photography. Filming was once due to start in September, it's believed, though a series of reports last week suggested it had now been delayed until early next year .

The Most Surprising Avengers and Marvel Characters Not Announced for Doomsday

"Once I finish on Broadway, I'll go to finish up all the Avengers stuff for Secret Wars," Mackie has now said, confirming that Secret Wars filming will take place well into 2027.

Again, it's worth reiterating the fact Marvel has made no suggestion that Secret Wars' planned December 17, 2027 will also be delayed. But fans are now beginning to wonder how the studio plans to complete filming (and more critically, post-production) on such a complex project with little more than 12 months left to go until it arrives in theaters.

Currently, there's no suggestion that Secret Wars will begin shooting this year, and much of the cast are expected to be busy from late November onwards as the Avengers: Doomsday promotional campaign really picks up. Mackie will then just have a short window until his time on stage for Macbeth starts. On the upside, shooting Secret Wars in 2027 will allow Marvel to respond to audience feedback to Doomsday, following its arrival this December 18.

Last month, directors Joe and Anthony Russo teased that Marvel fans need to prepare for "a very surprising ending" to Avengers: Doomsday , which has a "focused propulsive narrative," while still weighing in as one of the studio's longest films to date.

articles.title: 3 New Batman LEGO Sets Announced, Including Wall Art of an Iconic Joker Comic Cover
articles.summary: LEGO has announced three new Batman sets, including two Batmobiles and a wall art recreation of Jock's classic Joker comic cover.
articles.body:
LEGO has announced three new Batman LEGO sets coming out on January 1. Two are based on Batmobiles, and they include codes to unlock gold versions of the vehicles in the video game LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight. The other one is LEGO DC Batman: The Joker Wall Art, a set that recreates a famous comic book cover as a piece of art you can actually hang on your wall. It looks awesome, but also kind of terrifying.

LEGO DC: Batman Returns Batmobile & Duck

If you have no time for blurbs, you can check out all the newly announced sets in the catalog above.

I love LEGO Art sets because they look great (the art literally pops out of the frame), and because they’re functional as actual decorations for your walls. This set recreates Jock’s iconic cover of Detective Comics #880 , which came out in 2011. It shows a nightmarish close-up of Joker’s face, with a giant red-ringed smile, red Batman symbols for eyes. and the whole top of his his head erupting in a flurry of flying bats.

In the LEGO version, the bats actually fly out of the frame of the “painting.” It’s a great effect. LEGO promises “hidden details” layered under the surface of the artwork that you’ll discover as you build.

Those who remember Tim Burton’s 1991 classic Batman Returns will also remember a.) the awesome Batmobile from the movie, and b.) Penguin’s giant duck vehicle. This set lets you build both. If the recent, pricier LEGO Batman Returns Batmobile cost more than you wanted to spend, then perhaps this smaller version will suffice. As an added bonus, this set comes with a code to unlock the Golden Red Brick in LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight, “adding a gold theme for characters and vehicles.” This set also unlocks a “gold Batman Returns Batmobile Batcave Prop in-game.”

Fans of the now-classic Batman Arkham video games can also pick up this 317-piece recreation of the series’ chunky Batmobile. It’s all sharp edges and thick tires. It looks great, and it comes with a Batman minifigure, as well as a code to unlock gold skins and/or vehicles in the Legacy of the Dark Knight.

Don't have the game? It's pretty great. As reviewer Simon Cardy wrote in his IGN review : "Lego Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight is a lovingly made, often hilarious take on both Batman’s movie and video game history alike. It remixes classic moments from almost every film, with deeper cuts from the Caped Crusader’s comic book beginnings, too."

Additionally, if you plan to attend New York Comic-Con, which runs October 8 - 11, you'll be able to get a close-up look at all three sets at the DC Booth (#4365), where you'll also find a nine-foot brick replica of the Joker cover.

LEGO says, "Fans who pre-order the LEGO DC Batman The Joker Wall Art on-site will receive a reprint of the issue with a LEGO-brick-inspired cover, and original cover artist Jock will be signing at the booth on Thursday, October 8 at 11:00am ET."

For more, check out our roundup of every upcoming LEGO set announced so far.

articles.title: 'It’s Incredibly Sad Knowing That We Won’t Get to Finish What We Were Working on' — Hellblade Staff Bid Farewell to Ninja Theory as Layoffs Begin
articles.summary: After Xbox announced its intention to close Hellblade developer Ninja Theory, staff have started saying their farewells as layoffs begin.
articles.body:
Last month, Xbox announced its intention to close Hellblade developer Ninja Theory , after two deals to save the company didn’t pan out. Now we’re starting to see the consequences of that decision as people at the studio post on job site LinkedIn, spotted by journalist Chris Kerr .

“I’ve been trying to figure out how to write this because Ninja Theory was never just a job to me,” gameplay programmer Katrin Mair said. “After four years, it’s hard to put into words how much this place and the people in it have meant to me.

“What I’ll remember most is how much people cared. About the work, about the details, and about each other. I feel very lucky that this was the place where I got to start my career and grow into the programmer I am today. It’s incredibly sad knowing that we won’t get to finish what we were working on. So much care, talent and effort went into it, and I really wish we’d had the chance to see what it could have become.”

Senua's Saga: Hellblade II Review Screens

Mair moved to the U.K. to work at Ninja Theory. Elsewhere, technical director Loong-Wei Ding is among those affected, with his leaving post calling for other studios to pick up his Ninja Theory colleagues.

Expert technical sound designer Alessio Mellina is also at risk of redundancy after 12 years with the studio working on the industry-leading binaural audio that powered Hellblade ’s haunting whispers. “As the only Technical Sound Designer here, I've been the owner of most of our dynamic audio systems on recent projects,” he said.

Performance capture expert Xoe Suvari has also been let go. “Hundreds of shoot days,” he said. “Hours and hours of data. Sweat and bruises from set builds. New pipelines and the never ending battle of naming conventions. I saw my team grow at work and as people, and together we built a performance capture stage that was truly top of its class.”

All of the posts talk about their colleagues, suggesting layoffs are widespread throughout the studio. In June, at an Xbox Games Showcase event, Microsoft announced Senua , the third game in the Hellblade series. It’s widely speculated that the trailer was intended to increase interest with potential buyers of Ninja Theory, since Microsoft would have known at this point that it had no plans to publish the title.

Last month, Microsoft announced that the next mainline Halo game will be developed by Call of Duty maker Activision , with mass layoffs hitting Halo Studios. Xbox has moved Age of Empires developer World's Edge and Sea of Thieves developer Rare under the Activision umbrella.

Outside Activision, Obsidian, developer of Grounded and The Outer Worlds is now a Bethesda studio, as it begins work on a new Fallout game. According to Xbox Chief Content Officer Matt Booty, these changes bring us three quarters of the way through planned restructures, which suggests more job losses will happen over the course of the next few months.

articles.summary: New York has not announced its Game 3 starter. Aaron Boone has said Carlos Rodón lines up for Game 3 […]
articles.body:
New York has not announced its Game 3 starter. Aaron Boone has said Carlos Rodón lines up for Game 3 or 4 at Yankee Stadium, with Max Fried also available. The choice matters more after the Yankees dropped the ALDS opener to Tampa Bay.

Here is my call: give Rodón Game 3. He threw eight scoreless innings against the Rays on Sept. 22, a performance that deserves more weight than a rigid rotation order. He finished the regular season 7-3 with a 2.67 ERA in 16 starts. The left-hander is rested and already knows he can get through this lineup multiple times.

Yankees have a useful choice, not a fixed plan

Boone described the rotation as a good, difficult decision. He is right. Gerrit Cole started Game 1, Cam Schlittler gets Game 2 on Monday, and Fried gave the Yankees six strong innings in the Wild Card clincher. Nobody has been pushed into this spot because the other choices are poor.

But the Rays are not a team New York should plan around in the abstract. Rodón just faced them and kept them off the board for eight innings. If the Yankees win Monday, he can take the ball at home with a chance to put New York ahead. If they lose, he is the starter I would trust to stop the series from ending in three games.

Fried would still be available for Game 4, giving the Yankees a second left-hander and the flexibility to adjust based on how Game 3 actually goes. Waiting until the series reaches another difficult spot to decide which pitcher best matches Tampa Bay is unnecessary.

The Yankees already made their Game 2 choice in Schlittler . Game 3 deserves the same clarity. Rodón's most recent outing against this opponent was as convincing as any audition Boone could ask for.

articles.title: Modder Turns Diablo 2 Resurrected Into a VR Game, But You Probably Can't Play It
articles.summary: Diablo 2 is already a game you could lose thousands of hours to, but what if you could truly lose yourself in the world via VR? Well, a modder found a way to translate the isometric ARPG to a first-person VR game.
articles.body:
Diablo 2 is already a game you could lose thousands of hours to, but what if you could truly lose yourself in the world via VR? Well, a modder found a way to translate the isometric ARPG to a first-person VR game.

Reddit user fantasticauthor2736 created the mod , using an existing 3D conversion mod, FlatVR and BodyWalk. While the mod itself hasn't been published quite yet, there are a few videos of it in action, and while it doesn't look like a fully polished VR game yet, it does seem like a cool way to play the game.

All of the videos posted so far, though, have been in the first couple zones of Diablo 2, and while they haven't shown any particularly intense combat so far, it's easy to see how it works in theory. You just point your motion controller at an enemy and shoot fireballs at them. Easy enough.

The modder was also able to redesign the UI a bit , too. They moved the inventory to the belt, but the rest of the UI has been moved to the left wrist, where you can see health, mana and the toolbar. And, if you want to pull up the map, it looks like you just summon it as an orb that you hold in your hand. That's less ideal than the overlay map in the standard game, but I can imagine that'd make it hard to actually play in VR.

On the surface, it's hard to imagine how this even works, but it builds on the mod D2R-3D by emmericp , which just gives Diablo 2 some more robust camera controls. You see, while most people will see Diablo 2 as a 2D isometric game, it's actually all 3D. As emmericp explains in a YouTube video , all the assets necessary for a 3D view of Diablo 2 Resurrected are already in the game, it's just a matter of rendering it from the right point of view. Just keep in mind, that in the process of doing this, you won't be able to play the game without it crashing after about a minute.

To do that, he had to change the way projectiles were calculated, along with lighting and shadow effects to work properly when you're zoomed in. But once all the math is out of the way, there are still some bugs, like item names floating high in the sky, and targeting simply not working with mouse and keyboard.

The biggest problem, though, is that the D2R-3D mod will flag Blizzard's file integrity checker, which will crash the game after about a minute of playing it. He does explain that there is a workaround, but it involves using programs that could theoretically allow players to cheat, so he doesn't detail those.

Diablo 2 Resurrected - Comparison Screenshots

Fantasticauthor2736's mod, then, takes the D2R-3D mod and then further converts it to a VR game, using FlatVR, and then uses BodyWalk to let you use your body's movement to control your character's movement. But, even when the mod is released, it will likely have the same restrictions as D2R-3D, in that it'll likely crash the game after about a minute. After all, Diablo 2: Resurrected does require an online connection, and because these mods change the code in the game, there's no way to get around a crash without downloading sketchy software.

Still, it's one of the coolest Diablo 2 mods I've seen, and just makes me want a Diablo game that I can play on the Steam Frame . Diablo 2 has also been on the top of people's minds as we move towards Diablo 5. Game Director Joe Shely has promised a return to more methodical gameplay made famous by Diablo 2, and Path of Exile's Chris Wilson is hopeful that Blizzard's next ARPG will take more inspiration from the second game, as well.

articles.title: Prometheus Graft Is a Murder Mystery Starring Frankenstein's Monster
articles.summary: What happens when Frankenstein's Monster becomes Europe's most preeminent detective? Find out in this exclusive preview of Prometheus Graft: The Slayings at Death's End.
articles.body:
Mary Shelley's Frankenstein has inspired all sorts of great comics over the years, and a new Oni Press series might just take its place among them. IGN can exclusively reveal Prometheus Graft: The Slayings at Death's End, a new murder mystery that casts Frankenstein's Monster as an intrepid detective.

Check out the slideshow gallery below for an exclusive first look at Prometheus Graft: The Slayings at Death's End #1:

Prometheus Graft: The Slayings at Death's End #1 Preview Gallery

Prometheus Graft: The Slayings at Death's End is written by George Northy (Yuletide, EC’s Shiver SuspenStories) and illustrated by Caitlin Yarsky (Dead Teenagers, Black Hammer). The first issue features cover art by Yarsky, Eric Powell, Gabriel Rodriguez, and Patricia Martin.

Here's the official summary for the new series:

Decades after his creation, the creature once known as Frankenstein’s Monster has reinvented himself as Europe’s most formidable mind. After years underground, his scars have faded and his genius-level intellect has tamed his hulking nature . . . revealing an extraordinary talent for solving the world’s most inexplicable mysteries. Today, he is Prometheus Graft: gentleman detective, expert investigator . . . and something still not quite entirely human.

Now, on the cusp of a new century set to be ruled by science over superstition, Graft believes he his finally conquered his monstrous past . . . until he is summoned to the remote Romanian castle of Death’s End, where an immortal lord has assembled Europe’s most feared supernatural beings to broker a long-lasting peace. But their fragile treaty will soon be shattered when the corpse of one of the prominent guests is found murdered in the castle’s hedge maze . . . turning witch against werewolf and vampire against ghoul as suspicion and bloodshed spiral.

With only his instincts and a bloodstained trail of clues to guide him, can Prometheus Graft solve the slayings at Death’s End before a new day breaks . . . and all hell follows with it?

"I’ve always adored an Agatha Christie-style whodunnit and wanted to create a classic detective tale with a supernatural twist," said Northy in a statement. "But who to cast as the Hercule Poirot, Sherlock Holmes or Benoit Blanc of this monster mash-up mystery? Then it came to me: The Creature in Mary Shelley’s iconic FRANKENSTEIN was brilliant, tortured and a ‘living puzzle’ himself. What if he set out to try to solve the mystery of what he really is—and who exactly makes up his disparate, grafted-together pieces—and, along the way, discovered a talent for solving all manner of occult mysteries? That became our hero detective, Prometheus Graft. In his debut mystery, Graft is invited to Death’s End Castle to observe a peace treaty renewal between clans of vampyrs, witches and werewolves—but instead must solve a series of brutal slayings to avert all-out paranormal war."

Prometheus Graft: The Slayings at Death's End #1 will be released on December 9. You can preorder a copy at your local comic shop .

articles.title: Z Fold8 vs previous Samsung foldables: how battery performance, efficiency and display experience have evolved
articles.body:
With the annual releases of each new Samsung phone, it’s easy to lose sight of just how far things have come since the earliest foldables. As this year’s Galaxy Z Fold 8 and Ultra offer us their thinnest and lightest foldables yet, we thought it would be a good time to take a trip down memory lane and remind ourselves of just how far things have come.

Compared to previous iterations, charging devices from this range is something of a new experience. Despite having much higher capacity batteries these days (not a bad thing in itself, of course!), the upgrade to 45W wired fast charging (up from 15W) means you can now get up to 50% charge around a third faster, and a full charge in just over an hour, compared to almost two back in 2019. This is in part due to the switch from Lithium-Ion to Silicon-Carbon tech, which allows higher charging speeds without overheating, all packed within a thinner frame that helps keep things pocket-sized despite so much more on the inside.

The original Samsung Galaxy Fold arrived seven years ago in September 2019 with a 4.6” external screen, and a 7.3” internal. By contrast, today’s Z Fold8 Ultra offers the biggest ever 8” internal screen, but where it makes huge leaps is in its 40%+ bigger 6.5” external screen, thanks to a far better use of the handset’s real estate.

It’s not just a question of bigger is better though, as without improvements to resolution and pixel density these would be worth very little, but significant increases in both mean the phones of yesteryear can’t hold a candle to their modern day counterparts. Refresh rate has also doubled from 60 to 120Hz in the intervening years, offering far more fluid motion than before. In truth, those earliest handsets might have had 60Hz theoretically, but their ability to use it was limited in practice.

It’s also hard to overstate just how much brighter the displays have become. Even the largest luddite should be able to appreciate the original’s increase from 380 nits to this year’s three-THOUSAND nits is literally a night and day comparison.

In terms of gameplay, there’s really no comparing 2019’s original and today’s behemoths. The first Fold’s Snapdragon 855 processor and Adreno 640 GPU would struggle with graphic-heavy contemporary titles, with choppy sub-30 framerates an uncomfortable reality. By contrast, today’s Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 for Galaxy and the Adreno 840 can comfortably handle modern 3D titles at a stable 60 to 120 FPS. Hardware-accelerated Ray Tracing and AI-powered upscaling are something you can take for granted now that would have seemed impossible back then.

Performance has massively improved in this relatively short space of time, thanks to huge advancements in mobile chip technology. Improved thermal management means the phone can keep cool during heavy gaming sessions or multi-window work, avoiding any forced slowdown or stuttering to protect components. Huge advancements in AI have seen more and more squeezed out of the hardware too, with constant, iterative, and dynamic adjustments being made in the background to remove unnecessary workload from the phone and maximise performance.

It will come as no surprise to those who were there, that the original foldables were fragile and experimental. The visible crease on the main screen was the source of much derision but today’s models are virtually seamless thanks to titanium alloy film and the supporting flexible plate beneath. On the outside, there’s no more pocket lint getting stuck in the wedge shaped gap on your closed device and causing untold problems for longevity; the Z Fold8 folds completely flat.

If you got the 2019 model wet, it was almost certainly game over, whereas today’s handsets offer IP48 water resistance. If you were taking photos, you’d have to make do with 16MP, compared to 200MP today on the Fold8 Ultra. The latest foldables have also made the leap to 8K and HDR10+, unimaginable just seven years ago, whilst internal storage has doubled from 512GB to 1TB.

Whilst year-on-year iterations of Samsung phones can sometimes make it seem that improvements are marginal, it’s clear when you take a step back that the advances made in just a short period of time have revolutionised what we can expect from our foldables.

articles.title: How the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold8 has been optimised for large-screen entertainment, multitasking and all-day battery life
articles.body:
The recently released Samsung Galaxy Z Fold8 is both the world’s thinnest (4.5mm unfolded) and lightest (201 grams) foldable, but that doesn’t mean it isn’t tooled up for everything the most committed power user wants to throw at it.

Benefitting from both its 10:16 cover screen and immersive 4:3 main screen when opened, the handheld shapeshifts to suit whatever content you want to enjoy, balancing display immersion and multi-window productivity with its world-class power management.

For those who want to stream movies and tv shows on the go, both screens’ Dynamic AMOLED 2X technology supports HDR10+ content, offering true blacks and high contrast, with high peak brightness thanks to the 3,000 nits displays. The key benefit of the Fold of course being that you can take a big screen experience on the road, within a compact form factor that fits comfortably in your pocket.

Gamers benefit from this too, with that ‘2X’ referring to the screens’ 120Hz refresh rates, and that main screen’s 4:3 display offering greater immersion and FOV whilst giving space for games’ UI’s without them getting in the way of the important action.

What’s more, with the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 for Galaxy chipset under the hood, you can achieve high-end graphical fidelity without ever having to compromise on performance.

For those who want to tweak things, Samsung’s Gaming Hub gives you plenty of customisability options. The Game Optimisation feature in the Game Booster menu option, for instance, will allow you to instruct the device to prioritise performance. This forces the Snapdragon 8 elite chip to prioritise graphics rendering and frame rate consistency, which should both eliminate micro-stutters in the most intense fast-paced shooters and open-world action RPGs, and optimise battery life for extended play sessions.

There’s also a Labs feature which can force strict 16:9 scale where needed, to ensure games with less-flexible resolution options never crop critical UI elements from your field of view. You can even set up a Game Mode routine which will automatically activate when you launch any game, blocking pop-up alerts and activating do not disturb. We all love hearing from mum, but sometimes a badly-timed interruption can really let the squad down…

Much has been made of the Galaxy Z Fold8’s ability to offer two-way and three-way split view, thanks to the latest operating system, One UI 9. Whilst this may naturally feel like more of a business-use benefit, it actually comes into its own when gaming.

If you’re having trouble getting through a certain level, you can have video walkthroughs, map layouts or guides available right there alongside you without ever having to stop play. If you’re into something multiplayer, text channels, discord chat or WhatsApp can sit comfortably alongside the game screen to liaise and receive updates in realtime, without ever having to pause out. In the instances where you need both, the three-way split view has your back.

It’s also ideal for casual gaming. If you enjoy gacha games or idle RPGs, you can keep them ticking over while you catch up on social media or news articles, or even have multiple games running side by side.

All of the above would be no use of course, if you were having to plug in regularly, but the Galaxy Z Fold8’s 4800 mAh battery is more than up to the challenge. Built in AI software actively monitors your usage habits, deep-sleeping idle apps and dynamically managing power consumption to maximise the time you get out of it, without compromising on performance.

If you’re streaming video, you’re comfortably looking at 26 hours, so you’ll be falling asleep long before the handset will. And with gaming, if you’re not taking those comfort breaks every 45 minutes (we all do, right?) it’ll still go for hours before you need to charge up. And when you do, go grab a bite to eat and you’ll be good to go again - the 45W wired fast charging means you can get from 0% to 65%+ in just 30 minutes.

In short, however you like to use your phone for entertainment, the new Galaxy Z Fold 8 will help you to enjoy more, simultaneously, for longer, without ever compromising on the experience.

articles.title: Lanterns Season 2 in Early Development Ahead of Official Green Light at HBO, Co-Creator Says
articles.summary: Lanterns Season 2 is in early development while it awaits an official green light at HBO, co-creator Damon Lindelof has confirmed.
articles.body:
Lanterns Season 2 is in early development while it awaits an official green light at HBO, co-creator Damon Lindelof has confirmed.

One of the creatives behind DC's popular Green Lantern show offered the second season update during a conversation with Collider . Although it may not be the firm commitment to more episodes that many were hoping to see after Lanterns aired its first season finale, it's at least a sign that some of the minds at DC Studios are already working to will them into existence behind the scenes.

With Season 1 officially over and (most) questions answered, the main thing most fans want to know is: Where is Lanterns Season 2? Lindelof said he does "not know anything" about how the DCU's John Stewart (Aaron Pierre) and Hal Jordan (Kyle Chandler) may evolve in the future, but he did confirm that there are already "writers who are working on ideating on Season 2."

Warning! Lanterns Season 1 finale spoilers follow.

Of course, those who finished the HBO show's first season know that Chandler's Hal Jordan is well and truly dead by the time its final episode's credits roll. The topic of the DC superhero icon's death – and all of the controversy surrounding it – is something Lindelof also addressed as fans wait for Season 2 confirmation.

"I can only tell you that everybody in the Season 1 room," he said, "inclusive of the writers who are working on ideating on Season 2, felt like even though we knew that it was going to be emotionally devastating and/or disappointing and maybe even frustrating, that the worst possible schmuck-baity thing that we could do is show you a pilot where Hal Jordan was definitively dead, and then try to walk it back and say, 'Oh, he was a clone' or 'He's only mostly dead' in the Princess Bride vernacular."

At least as far as the eight episodes we've received and the greater DCU is concerned, Hal Jordan's final moments were spent arguing with Kelly Macdonald's Sheriff Kerry Kane on the bleachers of a high school football field in Rushville, Nebraska. Ulrich Thomsen's Sinestro did tease that he knows a way to bring Chandler's fan-favorite character back from the grave, but given it seems he's just starting his villainous ways, it's hard to take his offer to John Stewart at face value.

Lindelof really wants fans to know that he doesn't know what the future may hold. That said, he's also well aware that DC comics have been known to play with Green Lantern lore in the past.

"I do not know anything about the creative," he continued, "and I wouldn't want to hamstring those writers in any way for what future storytelling mechanisms they could indulge in. Knowing what the comics have done with Parallax — and Hal, I think, has died at least three or four times over the course of the canon, and celebrating everything that Kyle did in his performance to get the audience to fall in love with Hal."

Lanterns has been surrounded by theories for weeks, and considering we know the DCU Green Lantern Corps will return in the future, they'll surely only continue in the months and years ahead. Pierre, for example, is already confirmed to reprise his role as Earth's new Green Lantern in Superman sequel Man of Tomorrow when it premieres next year. Just how prominent his role will be, or how his potential part in the yet-to-be-greenlit Season 2 fits in, remains to be seen.

Chandler's Hal Jordan may be gone, but fans still love what they've seen so far . Some have even gone as far as to say the choice to have him play the character is a casting decision that rivals Robert Downey Jr.'s Iron Man .

While we wait to see if Lanterns Season 2 is officially on the way, you can check out IGN's 8/10 review of the finale . You can also read about how DC Studios' James Gunn and Peter Safran fit into a newly reorganized Warner Bros. and Paramount .

Michael Cripe is a freelance writer with IGN. He's best known for his work at sites like The Pitch, The Escapist, and OnlySP. Be sure to give him a follow on Bluesky (@mikecripe.bsky.social) and Twitter (@MikeCripe).

articles.title: Fortnite Has Updated In-Game Art After Fans Discovered a Google Gemini AI Image Watermark
articles.summary: Fortnite has quietly replaced a piece of in-game artwork after fans spotted its original version contained a Google Gemini AI watermark.
articles.body:
Fortnite has quietly replaced a piece of in-game artwork after fans spotted its original version contained a Google Gemini AI watermark.

Epic Games added the music track "Meow" by Ironmouse, Sleeping Forest & HalaCG to Fortnite last month, with the telltale Gemini watermark in the track artwork's bottom right corner. This lay mostly unnoticed until last weekend, when its wider discovery prompted something of a minor kerfuffle on social media and Reddit .

As of this morning, however, this artwork has been replaced with an alternate version (with no Gemini watermark). But after closer inspection, it's worth pointing out that the Gemini usage was present in the track list's original art that Epic Games simply incorporated in-game. Go check the track on Spotify, and the Gemini mark is there, too. In other words, the Gemini usage here is the fault of whoever made the track art initially — not Epic Games.

So, why the switcheroo? AI-generated artwork in Fortnite is a contentious subject for fans who have pointed to previous dubious examples such as an in-game poster featuring a nine-toed character in a hammock to suggest that Epic Games was resorting to poor-quality AI work rather than using human designers. A more recent, official developer video then pulled back the curtain on Epic Games' AI use, showcasing how the company experiments with AI in the conceptual phase when creating characters and in-game locations .

All of that said, Epic Games has always shied away from strictly confirming any particular in-game art is AI generated, and has maintained at least a veneer of quality over the evergreen battle royale it continually toils to keep popular. To date, there hasn't been anything quite as egregious as Call of Duty's embarrassing and grotesque six-fingered Santa .

The fact that Epic Games has made the switch here is, if anything, a positive sign that it does not want to openly show artwork featuring obvious AI elements, such as that Gemini watermark, in Fortnite.

articles.title: Why Fizz Is a Great Option for Phone Service Across Canada
articles.body:
When you’re looking for a phone provider, all the details you need to think about can make your head spin. What’s different about each plan? How does data work? How long is the contract? Are there hidden fees? It’s enough to make you wish someone would come along and just take care of all that for you.

Well, Fizz pretty much does that. It removes all those headaches by allowing you to create a plan that’s tailored to you. There’s no sifting through several different preset options to try to figure out which one fits you best. You’ll decide exactly what your plan looks like, how much it costs, and you don’t have to lock yourself into a contract.

That flexibility without long-term commitment is a big reason why the company has grown in recent years, now offering network coverage across Canada. So if you’re thinking of switching providers, here are some of the primary reasons why you should consider Fizz.

Everyone’s lives and priorities are different, which means the things they need out of their mobile provider are different. Many providers offer levels of plans that can require you to pay for things you won’t actually use, but Fizz avoids that by letting you create your own plan .

That means you can individually set the levels of your data, coverage, text messages, and call minutes based on your personal preferences. You’ll be able to see the price of your plan as you build it, and there are no surprise fees for activation, overcharges, roaming, or anything else. The price you see is the price you’ll pay, and as long as you stay on that plan, your price will stay the same.

Whatever plan you build, it’s not set in stone. You don’t have to sign a contract or make any other commitment. If things change or you realize you misjudged what you’d need, you can just change the details in a few clicks directly in your account, and your new plan will go into effect when the next payment cycle starts.

Fizz is a 100% online company, which means you’ll never have to call anyone or visit a physical location to sign up, activate, or change a plan. You just create an account on Fizz.ca to get started.

You can order a new phone directly through Fizz as well, with options that include iPhone, Samsung Galaxy, Google Pixel, Motorola, and more. You can pay upfront or split up payments over time, or you can bring your existing phone with you to a Fizz plan. All you have to do is check your phone’s compatibility , order your SIM, customize your plan, and activate your SIM. Or if you don’t want to wait, you can activate an eSIM for free. Fizz also offers refurbished phones as an affordable option that are fully inspected, guaranteed to work, and good for the environment.

If you want to make changes to your plan, that’s all done through your online account too. Just like when you first signed up, you’ll see the price of your altered plan in real time before you finalize, so there’s no surprises on your next bill.

No matter what plan you build or the level of data you choose, unused data doesn’t simply disappear . It automatically rolls over to the next month. Fizz also allows data gifting , so if you realize you’re going to be short on data one month, you can request some from anyone else on the network.

If you’re the generous sort and realize you’re going to have extra, you can gift yours to anyone whose plan includes data. You don’t have to pre-designate friends or family to gift your data to, you can give it to strangers if you want. However, it is important to note that you can’t gift rolled over data, just what is part of your current month’s plan.

Data gifting does more than just give you the satisfaction of knowing you did a good deed, though that part is nice. It also earns you My Rewards points, which is exactly what it sounds like: a rewards program . You can also get points just from signing up for a Fizz account, inviting friends to join, buying a phone, getting add-ons, or any number of other activities.

The more points you accumulate, the more you level up within the loyalty program. This unlocks upgrades and perks, like free mobile data, dollars off your monthly bill, as well as other discounts and benefits.

All in all, Fizz offers a combination of flexibility, customization, and ease of use that’s difficult to match. So if you’re thinking of switching mobile providers and want something that’s tailored to your needs without requiring that you make a long-term commitment, Fizz is worth checking out.

articles.title: Dungeons and Dragons: World of Warcraft – Everything You Need to Know
articles.summary: Dungeons and Dragons: World of Warcraft was announced way back in July, as the first Universes Beyond release for the storied tabletop RPG. And just like the MMO it's based on, D&D: World of Warcraft is absolutely massive.
articles.body:
Dungeons and Dragons: World of Warcraft was announced way back in July, as the first Universes Beyond release for the storied tabletop RPG. And just like the MMO it's based on, D&D: World of Warcraft is absolutely massive.

But while this was the first Universes Beyond release for D&D, it’s nothing new for Wizards of the Coast, with the initiative driving a huge number of Magic: The Gathering sets over the last few years. But just like the scope of the Lord of the Rings set for MTG, Dungeons and Dragons: World of Warcraft is an absolutely massive expansion, and almost feels like an entire game unto itself.

Rather than just taking the easy way out and releasing a one-off story module, Wizards of the Coast packed its World of Warcraft expansion with enough lore, dungeons, and professions that it could feasibly take you years to try everything. But, unlike WoW on your desktop, you can choose exactly how your Azeroth story will play out.

Dungeons & Dragons: World of Warcraft Images

World of Warcraft has been around for 22 years on its own, and the franchise as a whole has been around since 1994. Needless to say, there is a ton of lore and history baked into the world of Azeroth. And, a huge portion of it is built into D&D: World of Warcraft.

The entire world of Azeroth is described in the book, up to The War Within. And, just like the game, each zone has a rough level range that Wizards had in mind when designing them. As Game Designer Joey Haeck says, “WoW has a starting zone for Orcs in Durotar, so it makes sense for that to be a level 1-4 zone in D&D.” Likewise, endgame zones like Northrend (at least zones that used to be endgame zones) will be designed with high-level characters in mind.

Though, this is D&D, so it’s entirely possible to just shrug off these suggestions and build your own campaign the way you want to. Haeck says, “as usual, with D&D, the power is in your hands.”

However, the expansion is focused entirely on the planet of Azeroth itself. So you won’t find the likes of Argus, the Shadowlands or Draenor here, though you can rely on your own knowledge of those worlds. Luckily, Shadowlands and Warlords of Draenor are two of the most maligned WoW expansions in history, so I’m sure a lot of people won’t miss them too much. It does mean, though, that you might have to get creative to do a campaign in The Burning Crusade’s Outland – which is just a blown-up Draenor.

But it’s not just the geography of Azeroth. Wizards of the Coast also worked in all the major conflicts that have driven the story of WoW over the years. Principal Game Designer James Wyatt listed just a few examples, like the Alliance vs. Horde campaign, the invasion of the Burning Crusade and the Scourge. The Dungeon Master’s guide will suggest you pick three of these conflicts to shape your campaign, which will then help populate the world with appropriate monsters, adventure hooks and locations.

In order to make out-of-order campaigns make sense, Wizards worked in a brilliant reference to the game to explain it: Chromie Time. As Wyatt describes, Chromie will tell you, "Look, I made a timeline just for you!”

I asked Wyatt a little more about the Chromie Time setup and he told me, “The campaign I’m playing in right now (which Joey Haeck is DMing) began with us in Silvermoon City having just helped repel Xal’atath’s invasion, but then Chromie sent us back in time to the Classic era, where we might or might not change the course of history!”

Dungeons and Dragons: World of Warcraft – Sample Pages

One of the biggest parts of World of Warcraft is its dungeons and raids. And, of course, D&D: World of Warcraft is going to work those in, too. But, between D&D and World of Warcraft, dungeons are completely different types of gameplay. In the video game, you typically go in, barrel through all of the trash, nuke the boss down, loot and repeat. That doesn’t really fit Dungeons and Dragons’ gameplay.

Instead, the dungeons in D&D: WoW are environments where you’re expected to take things much more slowly. Rather than blowing everything up, these dungeons will have non-linear exploration, and you might need to talk your way out of situations, rather than relying on your DPS rotation. You might use stealth to just sneak past all the pirates in the Deadmines, rather than killing all of them.

Haeck describes some of the different ways players could tackle the Scarlet Monastery: “A sneaky party would have legends told about them, about how the Scarlet Crusade’s leadership vanished without a trace one day.”

In Dire Maul, the book gives a brief history of the dungeon, about how the ancient Night Elf ruin was overrun by Satyrs and Ogres after the Well of Eternity exploded and Fel magic corrupted the mages who lived there. The book also has a couple of example adventure hooks, where you can either go in and kill Tendris Warpwood, like you do in the actual WoW dungeon, or you can take a quest from an Ogre to install a new king.

Unlike the video game, though, there’s not much fundamentally different between dungeons and raids. After all, Wizards of the Coast isn’t going to expect you to round up 20 or 40 people for a campaign. What are raids in WoW are instead dungeons geared for high-level players, with epic boss fights. The example Wizards gave is Onyxia’s Lair – a classic dungeon from Vanilla WoW, which basically only consists of one long hallway that leads to Onyxia herself.

Each of the dungeons in D&D: WoW seem like they have infinite possibilities, and luckily the book will have a lot of them. Wizards of the Coast didn’t reveal every dungeon in the game quite yet, but the ones it did reveal look incredible.

Putting the Dragons in Dungeons & Dragons

Of course, the other side of D&D is the dragons, and those magical flying lizards play a huge role in both the tabletop game and World of Warcraft. But, while there are definitely similarities between the two, dragons in WoW are different to how they’re portrayed in D&D. For instance, Game Designer and Writer Carl Sibley described how he tackled the design of the Blue Dragons in D&D WoW.

“One of the cool things about WoW dragons is that they hold very distinct places in lore from the places in lore that D&D dragons hold," Sibley says. "So even though there’s a red dragon in WoW, a blue dragon, and a green dragon, they’re very different than the red, blue and green dragons in D&D for instance.”

With that different lore, comes different abilities, too. For instance, while blue dragons in WoW have a similar affinity to cold damage to White dragons in Dungeons & Dragons, the Blue Dragonflight on Azeroth are also masters of the Arcane. So, Sibley describes a blue dragon’s breath attack as both dealing cold damage, but also producing an aura that’ll interrupt spellcasters.

It’s not just dragons, though. D&D: WoW’s bestiary is vast, and it covers everything from Murlocs and Imps to the Lich King, all with the same level of detail and separated by challenge rating. Naturally, Murlocs are CR1 and Arthas is CR25, and should pose a significant challenge.

The bestiary will also cover some important lore characters. I already mentioned Arthas, who seems like one of the hardest enemies in the entire expansion, but Sylvanas, Alleria, Anduin and Thrall are all here, with full stats and histories. All of those characters have also been raid fights at one point or another, and their raid mechanics have been translated over to make sense in D&D.

For instance, when you’re fighting Jaina Proudmoore, you can get frozen in the raid by letting a debuff stack up enough times, which can end up in a wipe. But in the D&D version, Jaina just has the ability to freeze a player, and follow it up with an Ice Lance that can create a huge AoE if the target is frozen. Luckily, there are some creative ways you can get out of getting frozen, like taking fire damage.

Wizards of the Coast took the same approach with all of the creatures on Azeroth that it did with the dragons. Because D&D and World of Warcraft are both high-fantasy worlds, there is a lot of crossover in the types of creatures, but the things they do are different. So whether it’s demons or the scourge, a lot of care has been given to make them feel like they come from Azeroth, rather than from Faerûn.

Crafting isn’t new to Dungeons & Dragons, but D&D: WoW is greatly expanding it by adding professions, which are a huge part of the MMO. Crafting will work much in the same way, you’ll use your tool proficiencies to gather materials through gathering professions like Fishing or Herbalism, and then use something like Alchemy or Cooking to turn those items into potions or whatever else.

In World of Warcraft, crafting works by gathering up specific ingredients to fulfill a recipe, but the system in D&D: WoW is a lot more lenient. Instead, you just need to gather up a certain amount of ingredients, measured in GP, and then craft the item you’re trying to make.

The sample rules page Wizards shared does allow a DM to have more specific recipes, like requiring 50 Stranglekelp, but they’ll have to invent and keep track of those recipes manually in the game.

What’s new for Dungeons & Dragons: World of Warcraft, though, is that each profession will have a defined list of items they can craft. Those items, then, are gated by your proficiency in those professions, just like they would be in the MMO. You also don’t need to be a spellcaster or have arcana proficiency to craft magical items, you can be, as Wyatt puts it, “just that good of a blacksmith.”

Here are all the professions that Wizards of the Coast includes in D&D: WoW:

Anyone who’s spent a lot of time playing World of Warcraft, especially at endgame, probably has some kind of memories of endlessly grinding to max out your reputation in order to get new gear, a flashy mount or, these days, getting housing items. D&D: WoW also has a reputation system in place, but it’s much more forgiving, and won’t require you to fly around and pick up eggs for dozens of hours – if you know, you know.

From the early pages Wizards has shared, gaining reputation will do everything from making members of that faction friendly towards you to letting you gain an audience with that faction at the highest level. There are some incredible perks to be had too. If you’re exalted with The Horde, for instance, you can call on Sylvanas Windrunner or Thrall to assist you on one adventure. Finally, I can bring Thrall to the Broken Isles.

But rather than grinding, players will earn reputation naturally by adventuring. I asked Wyatt for a little more detail on how you’ll gain reputation with various factions.

“The Renown system in the Dungeon Master’s Guide increases your Renown score at a slow but steady pace," Wyatt says. "Your Renown score with a faction increases when you do something that helps that faction’s goals, which primarily means doing tasks they assign to you. So you don’t need to kill hundreds of monsters or repeat daily quests to get your Renown score up to the point where you can start gaining rewards.”

With most factions, you’ll start at 3 Renown, and you’ll become Honored at 10, Revered at 25 and Exalted at 50. Those numbers are a lot smaller than they are in World of Warcraft, but all the numbers in D&D are, and the rate at which you ultimately earn renown with different factions will be up to your DM.

Dungeons & Dragons and World of Warcraft are both massive games in their own right, and while I’ll have to wait to go hands-on with the new expansion, Wizards of the Coast really has worked the essence of the MMO into D&D. Again, Wizards probably could have just got away with releasing a simple adventure module that teleports players into one event of World of Warcraft and called it a day.

Instead, it really does seem like the entire world of Warcraft is here for players to explore, and in ways you can’t really do in the MMO. This is just one step removed from having a dedicated World of Warcraft TTRPG, and luckily we don’t have to wait much longer to get our hands on it. Dungeons and Dragons: World of Warcraft launches on November 17, right before WoW's 22nd anniversary.
