articles.title: Arc Raiders and The Finals Are Getting Adapted Into Films and TV Shows
articles.summary: Hollywood is mining Arc Raiders and The Finals for its next big video game adaptations, as the two franchises will be turned into films and TV shows.
articles.body:
Hollywood is mining Arc Raiders and The Finals for its next big video game adaptations, as the two franchises will be turned into films and TV shows.

Per Variety , Nexon, the parent company of developer Embark Studios, will team up with a production company known as Chernin Entertainment to develop adaptations of Arc Raiders and The Finals. As of right now, it sounds like the teams are exploring all possible options, which include TV shows and films. This will be done to help expand the worlds of these games that "reward the passion" of the players, according to Nexon.

“ARC Raiders and The Finals are exactly the kind of opportunities we’ve been building towards at Chernin Entertainment: ambitious global IP with the potential to become major franchises across film and television,” said David Ready, president of film at Chernin Entertainment. “Nexon and Embark have created visually stunning, atmospheric worlds that contain countless stories to tell. We’re honored they’ve trusted us to unite our film and television teams to tell those stories.”

Embark Studios says it will work directly with Chernin Entertainment to develop these adaptations, ensuring there is respect paid to the worlds and lore that fans have fallen in love with over the years. As of right now, there are no release dates or specifics for these projects, so they are likely still years away from materializing.

Arc Raiders was one of the biggest games of 2025, but it has lost some steam in recent months due to a lack of steady updates with significant content. Later this month, Embark plans to test a PvE mode in the game , allowing players to enjoy a more cooperative experience without fear of being gunned down by other players. The studio emphasized that there's no guarantee that this mode will become permanent, but it is exploring the option following demand from players.

Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

articles.title: Lanterns Cast and Crew on the New Green Lantern Oath and Season 1's Emotional Finale
articles.summary: Get the full scoop on Lantern's emotionally charged Season 1 finale and the origin of the DCU's new Green Lantern oath.
articles.body:
Warning: This article contains full spoilers for Lanterns Season 1, Episode 8!

Lanterns has ended its eight-episode run on HBO, with the finale addressing some of the show's most burning questions. How and why does Aaron Pierre's John Stewart become a Green Lantern? Is Kyle Chandler's Hal Jordan truly dead, and who killed him? We finally have our answers in what turned out to be a somber but enjoyable finale episode .

IGN attended a press conference where Pierre, Chandler, and executive producers Chris Mundy, Damon Lindelof, and Tom King spoke more about these key developments and the challenges of crafting the series. Why give John his own Green Lantern oath? Does Hal actually love John? Read on to learn more about the big twists from the Season 1 finale.

Lanterns Season 1 ultimately culminates with John Stewart embracing his destiny and becoming a Green Lantern. However, he does so strictly on his own terms. John wields Hal's old ring and pairs it with the fear-infused Lantern Sinestro (Ulrich Thomsen) forged for Noah (Shea Pritchard). He's a strictly unsanctioned Lantern who effectively blackmails his way into taking jurisdiction of Earth from Guy Gardner (Nathan Fillion). And to reflect this unique status, John activates his ring by uttering his own oath:

I'll embrace my fear, I'll do what's right.

Why introduce a new Green Lantern oath? How do these lines better reflect John's character at the end of Season 1?

"I think the idea was we sort of were taking a look back at what we had done with the season, and so John’s path was not the normal path," Mundy told press. "The ring didn’t choose him, he was interviewed, he was kind of raised for it. He was having to choose this thing, then he decided not to do it, and then decided that he needed to do it on his own terms. We wanted it to be true to the original and respectful of the original, but his version is rooted, obviously, in the OG version of it, but we also wanted to tweak it to talk about the themes that we talked about, and fear, and make it be a choice that he was choosing this thing and not something he was like, 'I’m doing it because my parents want me to do it, or I’m doing it because these things.' So, I think at a certain point, you end writing a season and you have a split second to look back on what you built and what was important inside of it, you hope people will like it, and it was our way to reflect what we built."

Lindelof added, "When you watch the totality of John Stewart’s story, it’s really hard to get to the end of it and say that he is in alignment with the Corps, with the Green Lantern Corps, and Lianna, and everything that it stands for, and for a man who pledged his loyalty to the military, to his parents, [that's his] idea of saying, 'I’m kind of beyond doing that for other organizations, and in order for me to formulate an oath, it has to be on my own terms and in my own way.'"

"What we see at the end is that John is not a hundred percent a Green Lantern anymore, he has a Lantern that has a bit of yellow in it, has a bit of fear in it. It’s an unsanctioned Lantern, as Guy says," King said. "And so, he’s not saying the same oath as every other Green Lantern because he’s not like every other Green Lantern. So, just like a Yellow Lantern says something different, or a Green Lantern says something different, or an Orange Lantern says something, this thing that John is, this utterly unique creation that he has not been given to him, that he is not chosen for but that he... chose for himself, gets its own unique oath, seemed to line up very much with the lore and where we’re going from here."

John becoming a Green Lantern in the finale is nothing if not a bittersweet moment. The act of charging up his new ring means all traces of Hal will be purged from it, erasing the Halogram and finally putting an end to the tumultuous bond between John and Hal. But just before the Halogram dies its final death, we're treated to a final, very poignant moment between the two. Both characters tell each other "I love you," a testament to the bond that exists between John and Hal despite the latter's best efforts to push aside his trainee over the years.

Chandler and Pierre discussed the challenges of acting out that pivotal scene and why it's such an important way of wrapping up their shared, season-long arc.

"The characters, they fell in love through this action and this friendship, although it was pretty rocky, I got to say [ laughs ]," Chandler said. "But for that moment to occur at the end, it was just such a human factor, and it was the thing that maybe a film in the '50s or the '60s and you’ve got the Duke standing there and he’s just not going to say, [imitates John Wayne's drawl] “Well, I love you, kid," doesn’t happen that way back then. But these were words that were actually expressed, and it was really nice to be able to do that, and it was painfully exposed."

Chandler continued, "The fact of the matter is it’s a human experience, and it was a purely honest, open moment for an actor to express themselves, and it was a joyous thing to be able to do on screen. And it was easy to do with Aaron because, although I really don’t like him very much [ laughs ], I knew I was getting paid, so, you know, the checks were [cashed]…"

"It’s funny because Kyle and I, so much of our dynamic in the series is tumultuous [ laughs ], and it’s volatile, and who knows what’s going to happen at any given moment," Pierre added. "And even in our personal lives, Kyle and I, particularly when we’re on set, we’re constantly digging at each other, we’re constantly trying to get each other to be the laughingstock of the crew, like this is going on for six months, we’re constantly doing it. But there are certain moments within the script that, I think for Kyle and I, when we realized that kind of stopped all of that for a moment, not that that stuff wasn’t thrilling and enjoyable and a bunch of fun, but when there were moments in the script that made us stop that and really lock into the emotional beat — that was really quite moving for us, I think, as the characters but also as the individuals playing the characters. And I think that’s one of those moments, and it was really very special. And Kyle believes he made me cry on that day, I think I made him cry [ laughs ], but we’ll have to let the episode bear and see what the verdict is."

Were There Different Plans for the Finale?

Lanterns Episode 8 defies expectations in that it's not an epic, action-packed climax to the season. The writers clearly got all of that out of their system with Episode 5 . The finale is instead a more moody, introspective affair that focuses on capping off John Stewart's emotional journey toward finally embracing the Green Lantern mantle. The producers were asked if there was a version of Season 1 that might have ended with more action and spectacle. The short answer? Not really.

"There was never a version of the finale that was more action-oriented," Mundy said. "This story was about these two guys. And so, we knew that if we landed it emotionally with them, we would have done our job. And obviously, over the course of the season, we knew there were going to be action things and all that, but... we barely even talked about it because we all just knew this is what we were going for, that that would have been distracting, that that would have been just incident instead of emotion, you know?"

Mundy continued, "What I love about the huge fist fight that those guys have is that’s a huge fist fight, but it’s like literally these two guys and it’s an emotional scene even though they’re beating the hell out of each other. And the ending had to be an even quieter connection of these two people. And so, if we were going to ask people from the very first second of the pilot to invest in these two guys and the relationship with these two guys, we just had to land it in their relationship or we wouldn’t have done our jobs."

For King, an action-centric finale would have been a "cliché" that would have turned the series into a lesser version of itself.

"I think one of our sort of sticking points from day one is no clichés," King said. "Avoid clichés like they’re the plague. As someone who consumes a lot of superhero content, that can leak into that content and make it boring and can give you the superhero exhaustion that we’ve seen a thousand pieces about. I’ve seen a lot of shows that end with no action and emotion. But I watched the finale today, I hadn’t seen it in months, it’s just the acting, to me, is more powerful, is so beautiful and so thrilling, and I’m on the edge of my seat the entire time in a way I’m not when I just see people clinging against each other and I don’t care about them. It’s not what you expect, and that’s entirely what this show has been and is sort of what we’re always going to do."

The conference ended with perhaps the most pressing question of them all: What happened to Hal's beloved pet plant Earl? The finale includes a flashback scene where Hal and Earl are trapped in a burning house. Hal falls into the basement and burns in much the same way John burned back in 2016, but he, too, is saved by Manhunter technology. But what of Earl? Did he survive the blazing inferno? Did he have to be reskinned, too?

Technically, we know Earl was fine, because he interacts with John followinng Hal's murder in Episode 6. But the attendees were still quick to reassure fans and point out that this little carnivorous houseplant is a tough cookie.

"That’s an excellent question that I’ve never considered," Mundy said. "Someone went deeper than we did, and we thought we went deep. I don’t think Earl needed to be reskinned; I don’t think Earl goes down that easy…"

Lindelof concurred, saying, "Yeah, I think Earl is pretty resilient. The botanical creatures of the galaxy can grow their own skin, I would imagine. Earl probably has the thickest skin of anybody on the show, I would imagine."

Basically, if there is a Season 2 — and all signs point to that right now — Earl should still be a vital part of the cast.

For more, see what James Gunn had to say about the criticisms surrounding Hal's death and brush up on every DC movie and series in development .

articles.title: God Packs are Officially Coming to Magic: The Gathering
articles.summary: Magic: The Gathering booster packs have gone through a lot of changes in the last decade, some of which have been awful. But Wizards of the Coast is introducing 'God Packs' to MTG, which could feel like winning the lottery.
articles.body:
Magic: The Gathering booster packs have gone through a lot of changes in the last decade, some of which have been awful. But Wizards of the Coast is introducing 'God Packs' to MTG, which could feel like winning the lottery.

Everyone who plays TCGs knows the rush you get when you open a booster with a better spread of rares and mythics than usual. Right now, in a Play Booster, that usually means getting between two and four rares and mythics, and it feels incredible when it happens. But in a blog post , Wizards is taking that feeling a step further by announcing 'God Packs,' which will be entirely comprised of rares and mythics.

Both Play Boosters and Collector Boosters will have a chance to be a god pack, with Collector Boosters naturally being way more likely to hit gold. Approximately 1 in 1,000 Play Boosters will be God Packs, and 1 in 300 Collector Boosters will be God Packs.

God Packs will have their loot distributed differently between Play and Collector boosters, too. For Play boosters, you'll get one special 'God Pack celebration card' – whatever that means – along with 10 non-foil Rares and Mythics. Then, there will be two non-foil 'Booster Fun' variants (think showcase and borderless cards), along with two foil 'Booster Fun' cards.

For Collector Boosters, though, you'll get one foil land, 3 foil default frame rares and/or mythics, 3 non-foil 'Booster Fun' variants, and 5 foil 'Booster Fun' variants. On top of these rare God Packs, though, Wizards says in its blog, "while we're at it, we're also increasing the drop rates on foil rare and mythic rare cards across booster packs" in order to make them more fun to open.

But it can't all be fun and games; Wizards is also removing things from boosters, like foil commons and uncommons from play boosters altogether. It's also trimming the amount of cards in Collector Boosters down to 12, by removing 3 of the foil common and uncommon slots.

Wizards claims that these changes will make opening Collector Boosters more meaningful, saying in its blog:

"How does removing cards make opening Collector Boosters more exciting? We'll be honest here—it doesn't. But we do know that most people who open Collector Boosters mostly skip past these cards. Not everyone, but enough of a majority. You can see it in virtually any Collector Booster opening video, where the video practically skips over that section of the booster. Removing them isn't about shrinking the experience; it's about making room—in terms of both printing capacity and player psychology—for cards people actually get excited about."

There are a lot of people who skip through their commons and uncommons when cracking a lot of packs, hell I do it sometimes. But there are enough commons and uncommons that see constructed play and already jump in price – just look at Aetherdrift's Stock Up – that I could see removing these uncommon slots having unforseen consequences.

Either way, these booster changes will go live when Nauctis: The Sunken Realm, and will carry over to every in-universe set going forward. As for Universes Beyond, those sets will get these new booster changes starting in 2028.

articles.title: Sicario 3 Will Reunite Emily Blunt With Benicio del Toro and Josh Brolin
articles.summary: Sicario 3 is reportedly moving forward with Emily Blunt, Josh Brolin, and Benicio del Toro signed on to return.
articles.body:
Sicario 3 is reportedly moving forward with Emily Blunt, Josh Brolin, and Benicio del Toro signed on to return.

As Deadline reports, the three stars are attached to return in a new installment of the gritty thriller franchise. Reports of a third Sicario have been floating around for years, but it has actually appeared to gain some momentum this year. Josh Brolin stated earlier this summer that Sicario 3 was happening soon, but didn't reveal any further details. Now, it seems the film has locked in its cast, a director, and a writer.

The film will be directed by Padraic McKinley, who recently helmed a drama starring Ethan Hawke known as The Weight. McKinley is an editor-turned-director, with only two films under his belt as a director. Sicario 3 will be his third project at the helm, and he will be directing from a script by Steven Knight, the creator of Peaky Blinders and writer of the next James Bond film.

The three actors signed on for a third film after reading the script, and it's currently being edited with notes from the trio. The actors also interviewed potential directors before eventually landing on McKinley. As of right now, the team behind the film is looking to shop the project around to different studios.

Deadline did not reveal whether or not Taylor Sheridan has any involvement in the project. He wrote the first two films, but it appears he will not be a writer on this film. Presumably, he will stay on as a producer, but that's pure speculation. The prolific writer has his hands tied with a number of TV shows and films, including a Call of Duty movie, so he may not have had time to work on a new Sicario film.

The return of Emily Blunt is also interesting, as she was absent from the second Sicario film. Her character seemed to have largely completed her arc, so it made sense not to bring her back, but some fans thought her exclusion made Sicario 2 feel more like a traditional, less interesting action flick. Having Blunt as part of the cast again may ensure Sicario 3 has more depth.

The film currently has no release date, but it certainly sounds like things are ramping up quickly.

articles.title: Legendary Japanese Solid Snake Actor Wants 'New Metal Gear Game,' But 'Won't Do One Without Kojima'
articles.summary: Solid Snake's legendary Japanese actor is keen to return for a new game, though feels conflicted about any fresh entry without the involvement of creator Hideo Kojima.
articles.body:
Solid Snake's Japanese voice and motion capture actor is keen to return for a new game, though feels conflicted about any fresh entry without the involvement of creator Hideo Kojima.

In an interview with Bunshun (translated by IGN), Snake actor Akio Otsuka reminisced about his deep attachment to the Metal Gear series and keen desire for Konami to make another entry — which may come as a surprise for Japanese fans of the series. Famously, Otsuka previously said he wouldn’t make a new game sans Kojima — a quote that spread around the franchise's Japanese fandom after the Konami/Kojima split.

Reflecting on that and his bond with the series' creator, Otsuka said: "My job as a voice actor is to do what I’m told. But when it comes to the Metal Gear series, it was created by Kojima, and I take pride in having helped bring it to life.

"So I [previously] said, 'I don’t want to do a Metal Gear that doesn’t involve Kojima.' Now I've said that, I can't take it back," he said.

Metal Gear Solid: Master Collection Vol. 2 February 2026 State of Play Trailer - Screenshots

Given Konami and Hideo Kojima’s far from amicable split, it seems pretty unlikely that Kojima will ever helm a MGS game again. When asked whether Otsuka had told Kojima that he’d like the Death Stranding director to make a new Metal Gear game, Otsuka simply replied: "I'll leave that to your imagination."

Looking back over his years of voicing Snake, Otsuka recalled that Solid Snake's famous "Kept you waiting, huh?" (" mataseta na" ) line was actually an adlib during the Japanese language recording. "It was subsequently used in ads too," Otsuka added, with David Hayter’s English rendition of the line becoming equally iconic.

Otsuka also recalled how surreal it was to have his real-life father, voice actor Chikao Otsuka, voicing Big Boss in MGS4’s finale, while Otsuka himself provided the performance capture. "When I arrived on set, my father's eyes widened at the sight of me in the motion capture suit, and he asked with surprise, 'Am I actually going to be voicing you?' It was rather amusing."

Otsuka expressed much fondness and empathy for Kojima throughout the interview. "He went through so many difficulties after leaving Konami yet managed to finish making this major game," Otsuka said, referring to the creator's subsequent project, Death Stranding. "After all, if Death Stranding had failed he could have easily ended up with debts that he wouldn't have been able to pay off even if he continued working for the rest of his life… So when the game was finished and they announced its release, I burst into tears."

Otsuka has also previously expressed support for former members of Kojima's team still working at Konami, who for various reasons did not jump ship to Kojima’s new company Kojima Productions. In an MGS cutscene-worthy bit on his Nameless Mouse podcast back in June 2023, Otsuka emphasized that, "I want the fans to understand this. I don't want them [the remaining MGS staff at Konami] to be made out to be villains. The people who stayed at Konami were part of the crew on Kojima's ship. These people, who inherited the director's legacy, want to protect Metal Gear."

Just as David Hayter is commonly held up by MGS fans as the definitive English voice of Snake (despite his controversial replacement by Kiefer Sutherland in MGS5), Otsuka's performance holds similar significance for Japanese fans. "I certainly have a deep attachment to Snake," Otsuka concluded. "After all, to the [Japanese] fans, Snake will always be Akio Otsuka, regardless of what happened between Kojima and Konami. When I think of the fans… well I'm really caught in the middle.”

While Kojima may be busy for the foreseeable future working on new projects O.D. and Physint, Konami clearly still has an interest in Metal Gear — something that may well lead to an all-new entry in future. Last year's successful Metal Gear Solid Delta Snake Eater reused Otsuka’s original performance from 2006's MGS3. However, it seems that the actor might be open to working on a new Metal Gear Solid, should Konami choose to make more than just remasters and remakes of the groundbreaking stealth series.

Verity Townsend is a Japan-based freelance writer who previously served as editor, contributor and translator for the game news site Automaton West. She has also written about Japanese culture and movies for various publications.

articles.title: The Batman Part 2 Halts Production as Matt Reeves Steps Away for Personal Reasons
articles.summary: Production on The Batman Part 2 has come to an unexpected halt as director Matt Reeves steps away for personal reasons.
articles.body:
Production on The Batman Part 2 has come to an unexpected halt as director Matt Reeves stepped away for personal reasons.

DC Studios and Warner Bros. provided a statement to Deadline confirming the news, noting that Reeves is focusing on a "family matter." The studio stated that it is looking forward to "continuing this journey soon." It's unclear if Reeves is expected to return to the production or if he will be replaced by another director.

"Production on The Batman Part II has been temporarily paused while Matt Reeves focuses on a family matter,” said the studio. “Matt has the full support of DC Studios and we look forward to continuing the journey soon.”

Reeve's Batman saga has been a herculean effort when it comes to overcoming obstacles. His first film began filming at the start of 2020 and was shut down by the COVID-19 pandemic. The film suffered multiple delays as a result, but managed to come out the other side as a critical and commercial success. The sequel has also been hampered by delays for largely unknown reasons, with its original date being planned for October 2025.

After years of setbacks, the film finally began shooting earlier this summer and looked to be on track to hit its early 2028 release date . Now, that is being called into question. Deadline notes that sources say it's too early to tell whether the production halt will lead to another delay, but it's certainly not out of the question.

Whenever The Batman Part 2 does release, it will star Robert Pattinson, Sebastian Stan, Scarlett Johansson, Jeffrey Wright, Charles Dance, Collin Farrell, and a number of other major stars .

articles.title: Gears of War: E-Day Runs Smoothly on Xbox Series S By Using SSD as RAM
articles.summary: The Coalition was able to work some magic on the Xbox Series S by tapping into the SSD to increase performance.
articles.body:
While Gears of War: E-Day is a beautiful game, it's incredibly demanding, whether you're playing it on the Xbox Series X or on PC. But, The Coalition was able to work some magic on the Xbox Series S by tapping into the SSD to increase performance.

The Coalition's studio technical director Kate Raynor talked to Digital Foundry and described tapping into the SSD while the Series S was out of memory. That's important for a game as demanding as Gears of War: E-Day, as the Xbox Series S only has 10GB of RAM, rather than the 16GB on the Series X.

Offloading data from the RAM to an SSD is nothing new. Your computer does it all the time when you run out of memory. What happens then is that the computer relies on the Page File, a dedicated block of storage on your SSD or hard drive that's used to hold overflow data. The problem with relying on that typically, though, is that SSDs are way slower than RAM, which is why your computer slows to a halt whenever it has to lean on the Page File.

The key for Gears of War: E-Day, then, was strategically choosing which data to offload to the SSD, and which data to keep in the faster system memory. According to Digital Foundry, The Coalition got around this by prioritizing data that wasn't used "in a frame or over a run of frames," while data that's constantly needed stays in RAM.

This approach does have its limits, though, and will degrade performance over time if the page file is refreshed into memory too often – as that does have a performance cost on its own. But, with this memory trick and dropping Lumen reflections, The Coalition was able to get Gears of War: E-Day running pretty well on the Xbox Series S. Hopefully, more developers are able to adopt this approach going forward, because I have a feeling that the cheaper hardware in the Xbox Series X is going to be more necessary as the RAM crisis carries on.

Gears of War: E-Day launched last week into early access, and has some pretty big changes over past games. But, still, The Coalition is proud that Gears of War: E-Day is now one of Xbox's main exclusives.

articles.title: Kingdom Come: Deliverance Dev Calls Out RPGs 'for Teenagers' That Just Focus on 'Power Fantasy'
articles.summary: Kingdom Come: Deliverance studio co-founder Martin Klima is "bored and tired" of RPGs that are just "power fantasy" trips "for teenagers."
articles.body:
Kingdom Come: Deliverance studio co-founder Martin Klima is "bored and tired" of RPGs that are just "power fantasy" trips "for teenagers."

The Warhorse Studios developer shared his thoughts about his least favorite kind of RPG during an interview with PC Gamer . Kingdom Come: Deliverance has received praise for straying from the beaten path in the past, and Klima's comments suggest that's no accident.

He admitted that the role-playing genre is one he enjoys. What he doesn't enjoy are the RPGs that set the player up to be "the chosen one" with a "grand task of saving the universe." It's a straightforward set-up that he's "bored and tired" of seeing, calling these kinds of experiences "repetitive."

"It's really a distillation of what the common RPG is," Klima said. "So, I found that there must be many, many people who are really tired of this formula and who want something new and different."

He continued: "The games that were and sort of are being made are still the games for teenagers. If you are 16, 17, you love playing these power fantasy games because it's something that you need. But the audience is much older today … everybody's going to think that I am hating on Expedition 33 right now, but that's definitely not the case."

There is no doubt a section of RPG fans who would agree with Klima's assessment. The question, though, remains: Why? He believes a reliance on strategies and designs that have worked in the past is to blame, saying major publishers are "best at recycling the same formula over and over."

Ubisoft is one of the more specific examples that came to mind. He called the "craftsmanship" of the publisher's games "excellent," pointing out that its games are mostly free of bugs and feature standout animations and character models. He'd prefer if that same level of craftsmanship was used on more innovative ideas, even if he doesn't have "any easy answers" for a company that could be taking financial risks when experimenting at that level.

"I played the original Assassin's Creed, and the original Far Cry, and the original Watch Dogs, and most of these games in the first iterations, and it was fun," he added. "But once you play the same game for the 10th time, it sort of becomes stale."

Klima recently commented on how he hopes GTA 6 will be able to "blaze a trail" for increased game prices . IGN reviewed Kingdom Come: Deliverance 2 when it came out last year and gave it a 9/10 .

articles.title: Miami Vice: The Final Director’s Cut’s Ending Invites a Darker Reading of Michael Mann’s Cult Classic
articles.summary: Miami Vice: The Director’s Final Cut’s rejiggered ending invites a slightly darker interpretation of the film than was evident in either of the past versions, especially when considered with what writer-director Michael Mann revealed about the fact-based origins of his screenplay at the post-premiere Q&A.
articles.body:
Full SPOILERS follow for all three versions of Michael Mann’s Miami Vice movie.

Miami Vice: The Director’s Final Cut premiered at Beyond Fest on Saturday. With the exception of the reordering of a few moments at the very end — and the omission of Nonpoint’s cover of “In the Air Tonight” — this version is largely the same as the Unrated Director’s Edition that was released on Blu-ray years ago. But the Final Cut’s rejiggered ending is enough to invite a slightly darker interpretation of the story than was evident in either of the film’s past versions, especially when considered with what writer-director Michael Mann revealed about the fact-based origins of his screenplay at the post-premiere Q&A.

Mann’s film version of the iconic 1980s TV series , which he executive produced but did not create, has been a love it or hate it affair since it came out in 2006. If you haven’t seen the Unrated Director’s Edition and are only familiar with the theatrical cut , then you will find much to unpack with this Director’s Final Cut when it arrives on 4K UHD and Blu-ray on December 15.

All three versions of Mann’s Miami Vice follow Miami-Dade P.D. undercover detectives James "Sonny" Crockett (a gruff, mustachioed Colin Farrell) and Ricardo Tubbs (a no-nonsense Jamie Foxx), who are recruited to infiltrate a Latin American narco-trafficking network after a mole has been discovered inside a joint Federal task force. Crockett and Tubbs sneak into South America by air and, once there, meet with sinister middleman Jose Yero (a scene-stealing John Ortiz). They succeed in insinuating themselves into Yero and his boss Montoya’s operation.

Crockett also falls for Isabella (Gong Li), a businesswoman who serves as the financial brains of Montoya’s operation. Crockett romances Isabella in the hopes of acquiring information (and she from him) but they soon genuinely fall for each other. It is not meant to be. She discovers during the climactic shootout that "Sonny Burnett" is actually cop Sonny Crockett. But Crockett can’t bring himself to arrest Isabella, instead arranging for her to escape via boat and start her life over elsewhere. All of that remains in the Final Cut, but the use of the song “In the Air Tonight,” the scene of Montoya’s empty compound being raided, and the very last shot of Crockett returning to the hospital where wounded fellow detective Trudy Joplin (Naomie Harris) is have all been removed in this version.

Mann’s Miami Vice was a legendarily difficult production, culminating in the abrupt departure of Jamie Foxx, who abandoned the film during shooting in the Dominican Republic, a move that forced Mann to change the movie’s ending . Mann never shot what he needed to end the story as he had originally envisioned.

Both the theatrical cut and the earlier Unrated Director’s Edition end with Crockett returning to the hospital where badly injured Vice cop Trudy, comforted by Tubbs, emerges from her coma. Although he let Isabella escape, Crockett ultimately returns to his police family in both previous versions. Closing those versions with a shot of Crockett walking into the hospital always made for an awkward ending, but it communicated that Crockett ultimately remembers whose side he’s on.

But the Director’s Final Cut instead ends with Crockett walking back to his car while Isabella flees before cutting to the end credits. The viewer is left to wonder what Crockett does next after letting a key player in their undercover operation escape justice. Mann’s revision of those closing moments suggests a reading of the film where Crockett’s future is uncertain.

In the Beyond Fest post-screening Q&A, Mann shed light on his reasons for revising the ending and why he wanted to refocus the ending of his Final Cut of Miami Vice on Crockett and Isabella’s love story. Mann also revealed that the tragic inspiration for his screenplay was an undercover agent he was acquainted with:

“I knew a number of people, one guy in particular who did very, very difficult long-term undercover in foreign countries – Beirut, Marseilles, Hong Kong. And I became fascinated with the dynamics of what happened when you lived a fabricated identity, but the fabricated identity in many cases becomes facets of yourself and it becomes performance, but there's only one take. You cannot make a mistake.”

Mann continued: “This was very much based on this one guy who had a family in Florida, wife and kids, and he was undercover working a money laundering operation based out of Hong Kong and fell in love with his target's sister. And if you met the targets, they didn't self-identify as part of a criminal subculture. They just were dealing in commodities. The commodity could be number three opium, it could be tapioca futures. It didn't matter. They were just people of commerce. And it turned his life upside down. It was a long-term relationship. And he was eventually indicted in Florida. And when he realized that he was going to get convicted, they would've seized his real family's assets under RICO. And he went out on I-80 and walked in front of an 18-wheeler.”

(Mann said this was the inspiration for how John Hawkes’ informant character commits suicide early in the film.)

“These (undercover agents) are very often men and women [who] are projecting the part of themselves that has not been manifested. So it's maybe part of themselves that they suppressed or it's been repressed,” Mann said. “They're convincing somebody that they could handle their transport or that this deal should go down and they sell and they're really good at it because oftentimes they're smarter [than the perps].

“And when they score and they become very good in this criminal fabricated identity, it is truly like a drug,” Mann said of how these agents can, in the parlance of Miami Vice, lose sight of which way is up.

In that sense, Crockett’s undercover persona “Sonny Burnett” is so convincing – he is able to seduce Isabella and eventually get her to agree to renegotiating his and Rico’s deal for a new percentage – that the character, in my estimation, begins behaving like an addict whose drug habit is worsening the longer he’s undercover. By the time the film’s final showdown comes along, Sonny is essentially a junkie in freefall.

“There often becomes a situation where (the undercover agents) don't go through red lights. There are no red lights. There's no red lights, no yellow lights, no green lights. There are no lights,” said Mann. “Maybe you look in a mirror in the morning when he wakes up and the guy will say that he is truly himself for the first time in his life.

“And particularly when you do what you're not supposed to do. They always say you're not supposed to have romances and bullshit. They wind up having romances. And that's basically, that's the genesis of this whole picture.”

Crockett’s romance with Isabella certainly doesn’t go unnoticed by his colleagues Rico, Trudy and Gina. While the latter two exchange looks of concern during a sequence at Yero’s club, Tubbs is far more direct with his partner. Tubbs’ concern is evident the minute Crockett ditches him for a boat ride to Havana with Isabella. Crockett assures Tubbs he’s got things under control at several points, but by the time they’re prepping their weapons for the final showdown he admits to Tubbs that he’s “with her 100%.”

Tubbs cautions Crockett that Isabella is “with them,” but Sonny is not ready for the collapse of his undercover identity where he will be required to bust the woman he loves. Like an addict struggling with their problem, Crockett assures those around him that he has his issues in check even as his actions and behavior indicate otherwise. His addiction eventually consumes him to the point where he can no longer do the job he’s required to do.

Miami Vice: The Director’s Final Cut is available on 4K UHD and Blu-ray on December 15.

articles.summary: Don't hold your breath for a new Watch Dogs game anytime soon.
articles.body:
Don't hold your breath for a new Watch Dogs game anytime soon.

As reported by Game File , Ubisoft CEO Yves Guillemot was asked by an investor about the future of the Watch Dogs franchise. The CEO noted that Ubisoft considers the IP "to be an important brand for the future" but neglected to explain how. Game File's Stephen Totilo stated that Guillemot suggested that there are no Watch Dogs games in active development at the moment, which suggests Ubisoft may still be figuring out where to take the series from here.

There is a Watch Dogs movie on the horizon , but there's no word on when it will be released. The film wrapped production two years ago and had reshoots last year, but there hasn't been any sort of meaningful promotion for the film to date. As of right now, it doesn't even have a release date, which makes it even more of a mystery.

Watch Dogs made its debut back in 2014, though it was initially meant to launch simultaneously with the PS4 in November 2013. Ubisoft hyped it up as a direct competitor to Grand Theft Auto 5, which released in September 2013. Unfortunately, many felt it was unable to reach some of its ambitions, but it still managed to make a dent in the open-world crime genre. Two years later, Ubisoft launched a much more impressive sequel set in San Francisco, but failed to keep the momentum going with its third installment.

Watch Dogs: Legion was released in 2020, also boasting ambitious ideas, such as the ability to control any NPC in the world. Unfortunately, the game received generally mixed reception from fans. Since then, there have been a lot of question marks around the future of the franchise. It seems Ubisoft wants to do more with Watch Dogs, but it may be trying to figure out how it can separate itself from a game like Grand Theft Auto 6 , which is set to shake up the genre in November.

There may be more Watch Dogs games one day, but don't expect them within the next few years.

Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

articles.title: Brandon Sanderson's New Sci-Fi Novel Is Included in Amazon's Latest Book Sale
articles.body:
Ahead of Prime Big Deal Days, Amazon has brought back its popular "3 for 2" book sale . A notable inclusion for Brandon Sanderson fans is the sci-fi author's latest book, Blightfall, which marks the start of Riftwake — a new series and the first official expansion to the Cytoverse.

Blightfall is less than $2 off on its own, so this sale is only really worth it if you can find two more books you'd want to pair with it. I'd recommend checking out Sanderson's Cosmere universe books, which are also included in the promotion as well.

Amazon '3 for 2' Sale on Brandon Sanderson Books

Isles of the Emberdark: A Cosmere Novel (Secret Projects)

The Way of Kings: Book One of the Stormlight Archive

Brandon Sanderson's Cytoverse is still fairly new. The universe was kicked off by the Skyward series, which focused on building a sci-fi world more grounded in the YA genre . During IGN's interview , Sanderson explained his intention to skew a tad younger with his writing "because the story is about teens who are forced, before their time, into leadership roles on a planet where war has claimed the lives of much of the older population."

Although the Skyward series technically "started" the universe, you don't actually need to read it to jump into Blightfall. Similar to the Cosmere books , this series acts as a new entry point rather than a sequel. That being said, I do highly recommend checking out Skyward as it's actually a terrific original sci-fi fantasy story. Plus there's already a TV series in the works for it.

If you'd prefer to listen to the Blightfall audiobook instead, there's currently a really good Audible deal going on right now at Amazon. You can get the first few months of the service for $0.99, which includes one audiobook per month. You'll also get a $20 Audible credit you can spend on anything you want

Although I haven't listened to Blightfall on audio yet, I do currently have the Skyward series on my list of the best audiobooks . Suzy Jackson is a terrific narrator in that series, and she also worked on Blightfall alongside Eddie Lopez.
